To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a model-based nonlinear control concept for a 4-axis pneumatic muscle driven robot arm, which is able to control the joint position and compliance.
a nonlinear model of the AirArm was developed and that the model was used for controller design.

the presented nonlinear model-based controller design concept for pneumatic muscle actuated manipulator arms is able to provide a good dynamic performance and that the presented nonlinear control concepts for the joints and the system level are well suited for this kind of manipulator arm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of a compliant manipulator driven by pneumatic muscles and the design and implementation of a nonlinear control concept.
the modeling and control design of the AirArm.
the modeling and control design of the pneumatic muscle-driven 4-axis manipulative arm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper shows the potential and the limits of the pneumatic actuator technology in comparison to electric motors.
the AirArm is able to perform the desired tasks and that the control system is able to cope with the requirements of a compliant robot arm.

the presented control approach can be considered as a successful example of how a complex nonlinear system can be controlled by using a model-based design approach, where a nonlinear controller is designed on a system level and then implemented in a decentralized fashion on the joint level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new concept for a 4-axis pneumatic robot arm, that we have designed a model-based nonlinear controller for the AirArm and that we have implemented this control concept successfully on the real robot.
the presented nonlinear control strategy is able to cope with the specific requirements of the compliant manipulator arm.
the presented modeling and control concepts are suitable for the control of a 4-DOF compliant robot arm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a nonlinear model-based controller design is possible even in the presence of highly nonlinear and time-variant actuators such as pneumatic muscle actuors.
the nonlinear control concept presented here is applicable to a large variety of different pneumatic muscle actuation systems.
the compliance of the pneumatic actuators can be used for the design of the control concept.
